claims.text: Nitrogen ion implantation followed by mild post-implantation annealing will produce a uniformly hardened subsurface layer in Ti-6Al-4V.
The hardened subsurface layer will contain finely dispersed nitride precipitates.
The treatment will stabilize a network of implantation-induced defects.
Nitrogen implantation at 50–100 keV and a dose of 1×10^17 ions/cm² at room temperature is the proposed implantation treatment.
Low-temperature post-implantation annealing will reduce amorphous damage.
Low-temperature post-implantation annealing will optimize nitride precipitation.
The modified subsurface layer will contain uniformly dispersed ultrafine nitride precipitates.
The modified layer will contain an optimized network of dislocations and residual lattice strains.
Nitrogen implantation creates localized regions of high nitrogen concentration.
Localized high nitrogen concentrations promote nucleation of fine nitride phases.
Implantation-induced lattice strains impede dislocation motion.
Annealing alleviates excessive amorphization and adjusts defect density to produce a balanced hardened layer.
The balanced hardened layer resists wear.
The treatment will increase surface hardness by approximately 40–80% relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The treatment will improve wear resistance relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V under room-temperature dry-sliding and lubricated tests.
Departures from the required implantation dose or annealing parameters may cause non-uniform hardening or undesirable brittleness.
The magnitude of the hardness and wear improvements depends on optimization of the post-implantation annealing process.
Long-term stability under cyclic loading and elevated-temperature service remains unestablished.
